text:
liz: quick sync: proposing an 'interface stitchdown' playbook for long-lived surface refactors. goal: let us incrementally remove surface area while preserving client stability and giving teams measurable debt paydown.
omar: what do you mean by stitchdown?
liz: think of it as an explicit three-layer process: 1) Guard layer: a lightweight shim that captures usage and emits migration signals; 2) Shadow layer: route a sample fraction to the new service/contract; 3) Cut layer: progressive throttles and final switch. each step has clear success criteria.
rachel: love the staged approach. two ask: how do we handle non-idempotent transactions, and what's the rollback story?
ben: non-idempotent writes are the tricky part. proposal: never async-shadow writes without client opt-in. instead for writes do synchronous proxying to new backend during shadowing, but keep the shim as the arbiter of truth until cut. rollback: preserve rollback toggles at infra with fast-path bypass.
chandra: operational cost is concerning. more shims + sampling + replay jobs = more pipelines. can we reuse existing proxy infra and sampling libraries?
liz: yes, reuse proxy infra and the sampling pipeline. the playbook will recommend sample caps (start 0.1%, double every 48h) and retention limits for captured payloads (7d default). we only enable replays for sampled messages.
omar: what about schema drift and clients that silently depend on swagger-nuances? we need a golden-test harness.
rachel: I can own a lightweight compatibility runner: replay sampled calls with both old and new implementations and diff responses. require <1% semantic divergence for stage promotion.
ben: metrics to gate: client-error.delta, latency.p99.delta, semantic-divergence.pct, queue.depth (if any). Also track by-client so we can pinpoint stubborn versions.
chandra: ownership split? historically infra shims get orphaned. propose: infra owns shim runtime, domain team owns migration scripts + compatibility runner. add a 90-day ownership SLA for any active shim.
liz: good call. add that to playbook. also add a bump policy: if shim is active > 90 days, domain must produce a removal plan with milestones or escalate to tech-debt council.
omar: can we embed a 'client hint' header so we know which SDK/version is calling? X-Client-Version + X-Stitch-ID.
rachel: yes, add X-Stitch-ID to correlate captures to a migration ticket. also include X-Shadow-Exp to tie to experiments.
ben: security note: captured payloads may include PII. must sanitize before storage and require a policy for retention and access. default to hashed-only bodies unless team requests opt-in evaluation.
chandra: testing: require each proposed cut to have an automated rollback job that can flip traffic back in <60s. no manual-only rollback.
liz: agreed. we'll require an infra toggle + a runbook with steps and owners. also include a post-cut smoke test suite.
omar: timeline and pilot candidates? I suggest pick 3 low-risk endpoints: /v1/health-check, /v1/model-profiles (read-heavy), and the internal metrics ingest endpoint. pick ones that exercise various shapes.
rachel: I'll nominate model-profiles and health-check. ben can we start the compatibility runner for those two?
ben: yes, I can have a prototype runner in 1 week. it will emit deviation reports and per-client histograms.
chandra: infra work items: 1) extend proxy to support sample-routing rules, 2) add retention + sanitize pipeline, 3) add emergency bypass circuit. ETA 2 weeks for basic pieces.
liz: action items: 1) I'll draft the playbook + checklist (ETA Wed), 2) Ben prototype compatibility runner (1 week), 3) Chandra infra spike (2 weeks), 4) Omar and Rachel pick pilot endpoints and owner contacts (3 days).
ops-bot: auto: created RFC workspace: https://rfc.redwood.local/r/interface-stitchdown-1881000000
omar: one more thought: include a small client-facing page listing active stitches and sunset ETA so product teams can surface to customers. avoids surprises.
rachel: agree. add a public facing deprecation dashboard + per-client contact.
liz: closing thread. will share RFC link here when ready. thanks! :white_check_mark:
